summary: Petition under Section 66 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 17 of the CERC (Terms and Conditions for Renewable Energy Certificates for Renewable Energy Generation) Regulations, 2022 and related provisions, seeking directions against the Respondent, National Load Despatch Centre, regarding the issuance of reduced Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) to the Petitioner for the FY 2024-25 based on the Renewable Energy Consumption Obligations targets notified by the Ministry of Power, in contravention of the statutory framework established by the Hon’ble Commission. 3. The Petitioner, IPCL filed the present petition under Section 66 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 17 of the CERC (Terms and Conditions for Renewable Energy Certificates for Renewable Energy Generation) Regulations, 2022 (REC Regulations, 2022) and related provisions, seeking directions against the Respondent, National Load Despatch Centre (NLDC), regarding the issuance of reduced Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) to the Petitioner for the FY 2024-25 based on the Renewable Energy Consumption Obligation (RCO) targets notified by the Ministry of Power (MoP), in contravention of the statutory framework established by the Commission. For FY 2024-25, the Petitioner claimed eligibility for the issuance of 4,40,119 RECs based on excess RE procurement over the RPO targets specified by the WBERC. During the course of the hearing, the counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the issue in the present matter was related to the question as to whether the Respondent, while issuing the RECs, needed to abide by the CERC REC Regulations or the Revised REC Procedure based on the RCO obligations issued by the MoP. After hearing the counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission admitted the Petition and directed the Respondents to file their reply and the Petitioner to file the rejoinder, if any. ## **Submissions of the Respondent, NLDC, on 03.12.2025 in compliance with the Record of Proceedings (ROP) of the hearing dated 04.11.2025** - (d) In order to ensure consistency and alignment between the REC mechanism, the FoR Rules and the RCO trajectory notified by MoP, NLDC addressed a communication dated 08.03.2024 to the Commission, submitting that REC issuance under the REC Regulations, 2022, required harmonisation with the national obligation trajectory to prevent differential treatment of obligated entities and REC market distortion. Along with this letter, NLDC placed before the Commission a Draft Revised Detailed REC Procedure (Revision-3) (Revised REC Procedure) for public consultation. Upon receipt and consideration of stakeholder submissions, NLDC issued a communication dated 28.03.2024 to the Commission, enclosing the Final Revised REC Procedure and stating that the procedure aligned with the Rules and the RCO Notification. The said letter informed that the Revised Procedure would come into effect from 01.04.2024, and the same was implemented accordingly. - (f) NLDC submitted that it acted in accordance with the statutory FoR framework and the RCO Notification dated 20.10.2023. ## **Rejoinder by the Petitioner, IPCL, dated 02.01.2026, on the Reply submitted by the** 9. Brief facts of the case: The Petitioner, IPCL which is a distribution company (DISCOM) in the state of West Bengal, filed the present petition under Section 66 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 17 of the CERC REC Regulations, 2022 and related 13. In view of the above submissions and pleadings, the Commission notes that the only issue that arises for the adjudication is whether the Petitioner is entitled to the _issuance of 4,40,119 RECs as claimed by it or only 3,20,826 RECs as issued by the Respondent, NLDC._
